# The host table and `mtr_in_t`: reference (ABI 1.2)

Everything a meter may use is in `include/tau_meter.h`. The player calls `mtr_pack_entry(const mtr_in_t *in, const mtr_host_api_t *api)` once per drawn picture; `TAU_METER(fn)` writes that entry point for you. Coordinates are pixels of the 400 x 360 screen, colours RGB565. The column **since** is the ABI minor that introduced the entry: a meter that uses a 1.1 or 1.2 entry must say so (`"abi": "1.1"` in `meter.json`); the suite fails a meter that does not.

## `mtr_in_t`: the inputs (read only)

| field | type | since | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | `const uint8_t *` | 1.0 | MTR_BANDS bands, 0..255, after the player's ballistics (fast attack, slow release) |
| `frame` | `uint32_t` | 1.0 | ticks since the meter was entered |
| `dt_ms` | `uint16_t` | 1.0 | ms since the previous tick |
| `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` | `uint16_t` | 1.0 | the rectangle the meter owns, in screen pixels; it never draws outside it |
| `bg` | `uint16_t` | 1.0 | the background colour (RGB565) to erase with |
| `force` | `uint8_t` | 1.0 | 1 = repaint the whole rectangle and drop every redraw cache (the context changed: new meter, new box, resumed) |
| `paused` | `uint8_t` | 1.0 | playback is paused or stopped: levels fall to zero |
| `peak_l`, `peak_r` | `uint32_t` | 1.0 | the loudest sample of each channel since the previous tick, 0..24575 (3/4 of full scale) |
| `degrade` | `uint8_t` | 1.0 | 0 full; 1 and 2: the player skips windows (every 2nd, every 4th), a meter may also reduce detail; the meter is switched off at 3 |
| `wave` | `const int8_t *` | 1.0 | optional signed waveform columns; NULL in the player today: build one from peak_l and peak_r |
| `rms_l`, `rms_r` | `uint16_t` | 1.1 | RMS of each channel over the picture's window, same scale as the peaks (0..24575); needs stats_ok |
| `corr` | `int16_t` | 1.1 | L/R correlation, Q8: -256 opposite phase, 0 unrelated, +256 identical; 0 when stats_ok is 0 |
| `centroid` | `uint8_t` | 1.1 | spectral centroid, 0..255: the level-weighted mean band |
| `crest` | `uint8_t` | 1.1 | peak / RMS, Q4 (16 = 1.0); 0 when stats_ok is 0 |
| `flux` | `uint8_t` | 1.1 | spectral flux: the summed rise of the bands since the previous picture, at most 255 |
| `onset` | `uint8_t` | 1.1 | 1 when this picture holds a hit (a flux spike against its own running mean) |
| `stats_ok` | `uint8_t` | 1.1 | 1 when the hardware statistics block is present (rms_l, rms_r, corr and crest are real) |

## `mtr_host_api_t`: the host table

Draw commands (counted against the meter's `cmds` ceiling, one each): `bar`, `blend_blit`, `blit`, `blit_abs`, `cblit`, `rect`, `rect_stash`, `sblit`, `scroll_down`, `scroll_left`, `text`. The convenience macros `mtr_rect`, `mtr_text`, `mtr_bar`, `mtr_scroll_down`, `mtr_scroll_left`, `mtr_blit`, `mtr_rect_stash` count for you; for the other draw calls use `tau_meter_cmds++` yourself or accept an undercount (the player counts the engine commands it really executes, not your number).

| entry | signature | since | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `abi` | `uint32_t abi` | 1.0 | the player's ABI: major << 8 \| minor |
| `rect` | `void rect(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint16_t colour)` | 1.0 | fill a rectangle (one engine command); the player clips it around fullscreen exclusions **(draw command)** |
| `role` | `const uint16_t *role` | 1.0 | the theme colours, MTR_ROLE_COUNT entries indexed by MTR_ROLE_*: read-only |
| `params` | `const uint16_t *params` | 1.0 | this meter's live parameter values, in meter.json's order: read-only |
| `stats` | `uint32_t *stats` | 1.0 | MTR_STATS words the meter may publish: [0] draw commands of the last tick (TAU_METER fills it); may be NULL |
| `text` | `uint32_t text(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, const char *s, uint16_t fg, uint16_t bg)` | 1.0 | 1x text, full cells (8 x 16 or the theme font); returns the x after the last glyph **(draw command)** |
| `rect_stash` | `void rect_stash(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint16_t colour)` | 1.0 | the same fill, not clipped to the visible frame: draws into the off-screen stash plane **(draw command)** |
| `blend_ready` | `int blend_ready(void)` | 1.0 | 1 when the bitstream has the pipelined blend |
| `blend_on` | `void blend_on(uint32_t a)` | 1.0 | source weight a/256 for the blits that follow |
| `blend_blit` | `void blend_blit(uint32_t sx, uint32_t sy, uint32_t dx, uint32_t dy, uint32_t w, uint32_t h)` | 1.0 | a blit blended with the weight set by blend_on **(draw command)** |
| `blend_off` | `void blend_off(void)` | 1.0 | back to plain copies |
| `mb_write` | `int mb_write(uint32_t pixel_addr, uint32_t two_pixels)` | 1.0 | the SDRAM mailbox, two pixels a word; 0 ok, -1 timeout |
| `mb_read` | `int mb_read(uint32_t pixel_addr, uint32_t *two_pixels)` | 1.0 | read the mailbox; 0 ok, -1 timeout |
| `fence` | `void fence(void)` | 1.0 | wait until every queued draw command has executed (bounded by the player) |
| `blit` | `void blit(uint32_t sx, uint32_t sy, uint32_t dx, uint32_t dy, uint32_t w, uint32_t h)` | 1.0 | a copy inside the buffer being drawn into **(draw command)** |
| `blit_abs` | `void blit_abs(uint32_t sx, uint32_t sy, uint32_t dx, uint32_t dy, uint32_t w, uint32_t h)` | 1.0 | stash to stash copy **(draw command)** |
| `sblit` | `void sblit(uint32_t sx, uint32_t sy, uint32_t dx, uint32_t dy, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t scale)` | 1.0 | a scaled copy from the stash into the drawing buffer **(draw command)** |
| `bar` | `void bar(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t lit, uint16_t fg, uint16_t bg)` | 1.0 | a bar column in one command: the bottom `lit` rows in fg, the rest in bg **(draw command)** |
| `scroll_down` | `void scroll_down(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t d)` | 1.0 | the box moves down d rows (a few copies, not a redraw) **(draw command)** |
| `clut_load` | `void clut_load(uint32_t start, const uint16_t *colors, uint32_t n)` | 1.0 | palette entries start..: load yours before your cblit calls (other users overwrite it) |
| `cblit` | `void cblit(uint32_t sx, uint32_t sy, uint32_t dx, uint32_t dy, uint32_t w, uint32_t h)` | 1.0 | palette indices from the stash at (sx, sy) through the palette to the drawing buffer; w <= 127 **(draw command)** |
| `scroll_left` | `void scroll_left(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t d)` | 1.2 | the box moves left d columns; the d columns it vacates at the right keep their old pixels (paint them yourself) **(draw command)** |

## Theme roles (`api->role[MTR_ROLE_*]`)

`MTR_ROLE_BG_TOP` (0), `MTR_ROLE_BG_BOTTOM` (1), `MTR_ROLE_SURFACE` (2), `MTR_ROLE_SURFACE_TRACK` (3), `MTR_ROLE_TEXT_PRIMARY` (4), `MTR_ROLE_TEXT_SECONDARY` (5), `MTR_ROLE_ACCENT` (6), `MTR_ROLE_ON_ACCENT` (7), `MTR_ROLE_ACCENT2` (8), `MTR_ROLE_OK` (9), `MTR_ROLE_WARN` (10), `MTR_ROLE_DANGER` (11), `MTR_ROLE_BASE` (12), `MTR_ROLE_CHROME` (13), `MTR_ROLE_PILL` (14), `MTR_ROLE_ERROR` (15), `MTR_ROLE_FAINT` (16), `MTR_ROLE_SPLASH_BG` (17), `MTR_ROLE_SPLASH_BAR` (18), `MTR_ROLE_FS_RED` (19), `MTR_ROLE_FS_TRACK` (20). The colours come from the user's theme and accent; use them instead of fixed colours so the meter follows the theme.

## What a call costs

The suite's cost model (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md`) charges 60 cycles for issuing a draw command and 12 for any other table call, 1.5 cycles per instruction, and 253 cycles for every 32-byte line of code fetched from PSRAM that the 4 KiB instruction cache does not hold. These are planning numbers, not measurements: the engine's own time (a big fill, a scaled blit) and the player's share of the CPU are not in them. The number that counts is the one the Pocket reports.
